title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Office of the Central Committee for Comprehensive Management of Social Security on Printing and Distributing the 2009 Measures for Incorporating Court Enforcement Work of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government into the Target Responsibility Assessment for Comprehensive Management of Social Security
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Office of the Central Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee

Notice on Issuing the "Measures for Assessing the Incorporation of Court Enforcement Work into the Target Responsibility for Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security for Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government in 2009"

Fa Fa [2010] No. 2

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Offices of the Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committees of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, and the Office of the Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Pursuant to the "Opinions on Incorporating Court Enforcement Work into the Scope of Target Assessment for Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security" jointly issued in December 2006, the Supreme People's Court and the Office of the Central Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee have conducted special evaluations on the work of resolving enforcement difficulties through comprehensive management in all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government for three consecutive years. During the evaluation process, courts at all levels and the Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committees and their offices have attached great importance to the evaluation work, organized and implemented it conscientiously, completed the assessment work on schedule, and effectively promoted the development of enforcement work, particularly exerting a positive effect on resolving enforcement difficulties through comprehensive management. On the basis of analyzing and summarizing the opinions and suggestions from all localities on the evaluation work, and in conjunction with the key points of the people's courts' enforcement work in 2009, the Supreme People's Court and the Office of the Central Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee have made partial adjustments to the assessment items and scores for incorporating court enforcement work into the target responsibility for comprehensive management of social public security for provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in 2009. The "Measures for Assessing the Incorporation of Court Enforcement Work into the Target Responsibility for Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security for Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government in 2009" are hereby issued to you for your earnest implementation. If problems are encountered during the assessment process, please contact the Supreme People's Court and the Office of the Central Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee in a timely manner.

January 4, 2010

Measures for Assessing the Incorporation of Court Enforcement Work into the Target Responsibility for Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security for Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government in 2009

In accordance with the requirements of the Notice of the Central Political and Legal Committee on Effectively Solving the Difficulties of Enforcement by the People's Courts (Zheng Fa [2005] No. 52) and the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the Office of the Central Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee on Incorporating Court Enforcement Work into the Scope of Target Assessment for Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security, the following specific matters concerning the enforcement work of the people's courts in the assessment of social comprehensive management work for provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in 2009 are hereby determined, along with the quantified assessment scoring method:

The enforcement work of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government in 2009 shall be listed as a deduction item in the comprehensive management of social public security assessment items, with a maximum deduction of 2 points.

1. If the Party committee, people's congress, or government fails to pay sufficient attention to or support enforcement work and the resolution of enforcement difficulties, or fails to formulate implementation opinions on strengthening enforcement work and resolving enforcement difficulties, 0.2 points shall be deducted.

2. If no working rules for the joint meeting on resolving enforcement difficulties have been formulated, 0.1 points shall be deducted; if the joint meeting fails to play a role in major enforcement cases that may affect social stability, sensitive cases, cases of illegal interference, or problems encountered in enforcement work that are difficult for the people's courts themselves to resolve, 0.2 points shall be deducted.

3. If insufficient importance is attached to the establishment of the linkage mechanism for the people's courts' enforcement work, and no countersigned document on the enforcement linkage mechanism has been issued, 0.2 points shall be deducted; if there are relevant regulations or documents in the region that contradict the law and create obstacles to the enforcement work of the people's courts, 0.1 points shall be deducted.

4. If state organs, people's congress deputies, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, or other special subjects refuse to perform the obligations determined by effective legal instruments, leading to mass incidents, 0.2 points shall be deducted.

5. If public security or procuratorial organs fail to promptly examine and handle cases suspected of refusing to enforce judgments or rulings and violent resistance to law enforcement that obstructs official duties, which have been transferred by the people's courts, 0.1 points shall be deducted; if this leads to incidents affecting social stability, an additional 0.1 points shall be deducted.

6. If enforcement by courts from other provinces or cities is not assisted in a timely manner or assistance is ineffective, and there is local protectionism, 0.1 points shall be deducted.

7. If a serious incident of violent resistance to law enforcement occurs in the region, resulting in casualties, property damage, or serious obstruction of enforcement due to improper handling, 0.3 points shall be deducted; if such incidents occur multiple times, or if they are not reported in a timely manner or are concealed as required, an additional 0.2 points shall be deducted.

8. If the case entry rate in the National Court Enforcement Case Information Management System fails to reach 90%, 0.1 points shall be deducted.

9. If no enforcement relief system for the particularly disadvantaged group has been established, and the government has not provided funding sources for relief for the particularly disadvantaged group in court enforcement, 0.1 points shall be deducted.

These measures are applicable to the assessment by the Office of the Central Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee of the incorporation of enforcement work into comprehensive management of social public security for all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government. The Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committees and their offices in all localities may, in light of the actual conditions of their own regions, formulate implementation rules for assessing enforcement work within their jurisdiction.

Each High People's Court shall submit assessment scoring opinions on the incorporation of enforcement work into comprehensive management of social public security for its own province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for 2009 (and may also express opinions and suggestions on scoring matters for other provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government) to the Supreme People's Court by the end of January 2010. After comprehensive balancing by the Supreme People's Court, the final assessment results shall be jointly determined with the Office of the Central Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security Committee.
